title: LUA-16 stack_trace fix requires a custom errfunc, not debug.traceback -- the debug library is intentionally never opened in the sandbox
symptom: ScriptErrorPayload.stack_trace is always empty for real LuaJIT 2.1 runtime errors because executor.zig's lua_pcall(L, 0, 1, 0) call (line ~543) passes errfunc=0 -- no message handler is installed, so by the time captureStackTrace runs after lua_pcall returns, the erroring Lua call frames have already unwound and lua_getstack(level=0) returns 0.
root_cause:
Confirmed by direct source inspection (not just the issue text):

1. src/lua/executor.zig:543 -- `const call_status = bindings.lua_pcall(L, 0, 1, 0);` -- errfunc is literally 0.
2. src/lua/executor.zig:585 -- `captureStackTrace(L, context.allocator)` is called AFTER lua_pcall has already returned (i.e. after the C call frame that invoked the failing script has unwound). The Lua Reference Manual's lua_pcall 'message handler' semantics: a message handler, if installed, must be pushed onto the Lua stack BEFORE the function-to-be-called (and its arguments); its absolute stack index is then passed as lua_pcall's 4th argument. If errfunc is 0, no handler runs. If installed, the handler is invoked with the raw error object as its argument AT THE MOMENT the error is raised, while the offending call frames are still live -- its return value becomes the error object lua_pcall ultimately returns to the caller. This is precisely the mechanism captureStackTrace needs to be invoked through, not called standalone after the fact.
3. captureStackTrace itself (executor.zig:701) is not buggy -- TC-ISS-0625-LUA-16-02 (src/lua/iss0625_lua_12_15_16_test.zig ~L272) correctly documents/tests that it legitimately returns empty on an idle stack (no active call). That test must keep passing unchanged.
4. CORRECTION to GH-595's own filed body: the issue text (and a comment already embedded in tests/integration/iss0625_lua_12_15_16_test.zig ~L561-566) suggests installing Lua's own `debug.traceback` as the errfunc. This is NOT viable as filed: src/lua/stdlib.zig's loadSafeStdlib (SBX-1, invariant documented at file top: 'Never opened: io, os, package, debug, jit, ffi, bit, coroutine') never calls luaopen_debug -- the debug library is deliberately absent from the sandboxed Lua state for security reasons (host_context.zig's registry-channel design relies on `debug` being unreachable to scripts). `debug.traceback` is therefore NOT a global inside the sandbox and cannot be looked up via lua_getglobal. The fix needs either (a) a small Zig/C `lua_CFunction` closure installed via lua_pushcclosure that internally calls the same lua_getstack/lua_getinfo walk captureStackTrace already implements (reusing captureStackTrace's logic while frames are still live, from inside the message-handler callback, then pushing the resulting string as the return value), or (b) opening ONLY the debug library's traceback function via a scoped/private registration that never exposes `debug` as a reachable global to script code (higher risk, more surface, not recommended). Option (a) is the design-preferred path -- it needs zero stdlib exposure changes and reuses proven code.
5. lua_pushcclosure and lua_getglobal are already bound in src/lua/luajit_bindings.zig (lines 134 and 228 respectively) -- both usable as-is; no new binding required to build a custom handler. lua_pcall's binding (line 169) already accepts the errfunc parameter; only the call site's 4th argument (currently hardcoded 0) needs to become the message handler's stack index, and the handler closure needs to be pushed onto the stack BEFORE luaL_loadbuffer's compiled chunk is pushed for calling (ordering: push handler first -> note its absolute stack index -> push chunk -> lua_pcall(L, 0, 1, handler_index)).
6. Interaction check with LUA-08/09/10 (instruction limiter / memory limiter / watchdog, GH-495/PR#593, same session): (a) MemoryLimiter.alloc (wired via lua_newstate) is orthogonal -- it only intercepts allocation calls, never touches the pcall error path. (b) The watchdog (timeout.zig WatchdogState/WatchdogHandle) runs on a SEPARATE std.Thread that never calls any lua_* function and never touches L directly (per timeout.zig's own docstring) -- it only sets a flag the in-VM hook polls, so it has zero direct interaction with lua_pcall's errfunc mechanism. (c) The instruction/timeout count hook (instruction_limiter.zig hookCallback, installed via lua_sethook/LUA_MASKCOUNT) DOES interact: when it trips, raiseLimit() calls lua_pushstring + lua_error(L), and lua_error is the SAME longjmp-based unwind mechanism a genuine script runtime error uses -- it unwinds through the nearest enclosing lua_pcall exactly like any other Lua error. This means once an errfunc is installed, limiter-triggered errors (instruction limit / wall-clock timeout exceeded) will ALSO now invoke the new message handler and produce a captured stack trace, not just organic script bugs. This is not a conflict or a bug -- it is a (likely welcome) side effect the design should note explicitly, since a limiter-triggered ScriptErrorPayload getting a non-empty stack_trace for the first time is an observable behavior change beyond GH-595's literal ask, and the design should state whether that is in-scope/desired (probably yes, more diagnostic value) or something to suppress.
acceptance_criteria: Design specifies a custom C message-handler closure (lua_CFunction via lua_pushcclosure) reusing captureStackTrace's lua_getstack/lua_getinfo walk logic, invoked from inside the handler while frames are still live -- NOT debug.traceback, since the debug library is intentionally never opened (stdlib.zig SBX-1)

Design specifies exact push ordering: handler pushed onto the stack BEFORE the compiled chunk (from luaL_loadbuffer) is pushed for the call, with the handler's absolute stack index captured and passed as lua_pcall's errfunc argument (replacing the current hardcoded 0 at executor.zig:543)
Design confirms TC-ISS-0625-LUA-16-02 (idle-stack, unit test) keeps passing unchanged -- only the live-error path changes

Design specifies flipping TC-ISS-0625-LUA-16-int-01's final assertion from `payload.stack_trace.len == 0` to `> 0` and updating its stale test name/comments (currently titled 'KKNOWN LIMITATION: trace empty on LuaJIT 2.1' and its body cites 'the proper fix is to install a debug.traceback function' -- both need correcting to match the actual fix)

Design explicitly addresses the instruction-limiter/watchdog interaction: raiseLimit()'s lua_error() calls will now also flow through the new errfunc and produce non-empty stack traces for limiter-triggered ScriptErrorPayloads -- state whether this is accepted as in-scope, additional diagnostic value, or whether it needs to be special-cased to preserve current behavior for limiter-triggered errors
No change to LUA-15 explicit-failure path (host_context.readExplicitFailure), which is read before stack-trace capture and does not go through captureStackTrace at all
notes: This ISS file supplements GH-595 rather than duplicating it -- GH-595 is the tracking issue (already filed, already has a github_issue URL) but its own filed body incorrectly assumes debug.traceback is reachable inside the sandbox. That correction, plus the limiter-interaction finding, is the value this diagnosis pass adds beyond what GH-595 already said.
